name: TerarkDB
tagline: ByteDance's RocksDB-compatible key-value engine built around Terark's searchable compression.
description: TerarkDB began at the Chinese startup Terark, whose searchable compression lets the engine serve point and range reads directly from compressed data, and continued at ByteDance after it took over the technology. Forked from RocksDB 5.18.3 and open-sourced under Apache 2.0 in December 2020, it keeps RocksDB's API while adding the TerarkZipTable SST format and compaction changes aimed at lower tail latency and better compression, with published benchmarks against RocksDB 6.12. It is production-tested only on Linux, and data migrated from RocksDB cannot be moved back. The last tagged release is 1.3.6 (January 2021) and the repository now gets only occasional fixes.
statusNote: No tagged release since 1.3.6 (January 2021); the repo receives only occasional build and doc fixes. RocksDB or Speedb are more actively maintained.

scale.notes: Embedded single-node engine; distribution is up to the system built on top.

strengths: Drop-in RocksDB API, so existing RocksDB applications can switch
Searchable compression serves reads from compressed data
Published benchmarks show better throughput and tail latency than RocksDB 6.12 on heavy writes
Used inside ByteDance, which tuned it for tail latency
weaknesses: Forked from an old RocksDB release and lags upstream features
Linux-only for production; bindings beyond C/C++ are not fully tested
One-way migration: data cannot go back to RocksDB
useCases: Replacing RocksDB where tail latency and compression matter
Storage engine for large key-value services on Linux
notIdealFor: Teams that need upstream RocksDB features and fixes
